page: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the n4 server family. It features 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel cores with hyper-threading enabled, providing a dedicated CPU allocation. The instance is configured with 16 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It operates on the x86_64 architecture and includes an Intel processor with 48 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and a large 260 MB L3 cache. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance type, and it includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks reveal a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core execution, such as stress-ng single-core CPU performance at 1561.99 and Geekbench single-core score at 1807.0, falls within the average range. Similarly, single-threaded gzip compression at 28.23 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 12.03 GB/sec show moderate throughput. However, multi-core and memory-bound operations are consistently weak, placing in the bottom 25% of benchmarks. This includes the Geekbench multi-core score of 4100.0, Passmark CPU score of 6010.98, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 22.69 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with uncached large block reads at 32.36 GB/sec and writes at 21.01 GB/sec.

Despite the multi-core performance limitations, the underlying Intel hardware supports advanced instruction sets, including Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and integer operations, alongside hardware-accelerated cryptography. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the n4-standard-4 offers a standard resource density suitable for entry-level general-purpose workloads that do not demand high memory bandwidth or sustained multi-threaded compute. It is best suited for static web serving, light text processing, and basic single-threaded application tasks, while being less optimal for database operations, software compilation, or intensive multi-threaded processing.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-4 is an x86_64 general-purpose virtual machine featuring 4 vCPUs and 16 GB of RAM, powered by a dedicated Intel processor with 2 physical cores and hyper-threading. The hardware includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX for matrix operations. It does not include local storage or GPUs. Benchmark data indicates average single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1807.0 and stable static web serving throughput of 6.53 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory-bound tasks perform weakly, as evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 4100.0 and low uncached memory bandwidth. This instance is qualitatively cost-effective for lighter, single-threaded workloads, static web serving, and basic text processing, but is less suited for heavy database operations or intensive multi-threaded compilation.
